[P1] [CORE-001] sailang/frame.py::Batch.parse + sailang/__init__.py exports + saimail/acceptance.py::receive
REPAIR: make receiver acceptance a required capability for raw-wire binding rather than a convention. Remove or internalize the public `Batch.parse(text, Profile)` binding route, or require an opaque accepted-profile token/capability minted only by ProfileRegistry.resolve/receive. Producer-side Profile construction may remain public, but possession of a Profile alone must not authorize decoding untrusted external wire into TriageFrame/TriageView. Preserve the existing canonical frame/record ABI and avoid documentation-only enforcement.
VERIFY: add an exported-API regression that builds an unaccepted hostile Profile plus valid wire and proves every normal public route refuses to produce a bound/decodeable TriageView until the receiver registry accepts that profile. Explicitly cover `sailang.Batch`, package exports, and any compatibility parser retained after repair. Existing profile-acceptance, frame, record, and semantic ABI tests must remain green.

REPAIR: make VerifiedEnvelope unforgeable through the normal public API. REPAIR: require derivative integrity verification before read_span returns any RESOLVED bytes. The narrow repair is to invoke verify_derivative(record, derivative_body) before span resolution. SRC-062:R005.text:
[P1] [W2-001] lab/saifren_run.py::Runner.call
REPAIR: determine send-call capability before the first dispatch, not by retrying after an exception. Normalize injected send functions at Runner construction or through an explicit adapter so each logical call executes the callback exactly once. Keep transport failures as an explicit result/error class emitted by HttpTransport rather than inferring transport health from `http_status is None`. A callback/programming exception may be recorded as HARNESS_ERROR, but it must not trigger a second dispatch and must not increment the consecutive gateway-transport failure counter unless it was explicitly classified as transport failure.
VERIFY: add a callback accepting only `prompt` and prove it works with exactly one invocation; add a callback accepting `model` that records one invocation then raises TypeError and prove Runner returns one ERROR with one budget spend and no retry; add repeated ValueError/HARNESS_ERROR calls and prove they do not produce GATEWAY_UNREACHABLE; retain the existing consecutive genuine transport-failure stop test and all lab contract tests.
